key_insight: The paper turns hyperfine intermediate states from a liability into an asset, using them to speed up and stabilize adiabatic CNOT gates in Rydberg-atom systems.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to higher-fidelity quantum gates that fit within coherence-time limits, which is important for scalable quantum hardware.
method: Use an EIT-based adiabatic CNOT protocol in atomic hyperfine intermediate states.
Optimize pulse shapes to improve both STAY-path adiabaticity and TRANSFER-path population transfer.
Extend the model to include decay from multiple intermediate states and arbitrary state numbers.
evidence_signal: In realistic Cs atomic setups, the optimized protocol achieves gate fidelities above 0.9991 in 0.3903 μs.
watch_item: Performance depends on controlling decay from intermediate hyperfine states, so implementation must carefully manage loss channels and pulse-optimization accuracy.
paper_title: Fast Adiabatic Quantum Gates via Hyperfine Intermediate States
